# Aunt Euphemia

## Overview

- **Age:** around fifty years old  <sub>[v1 c26 P0](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0000)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c26 P0](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0000), [v1 c29 P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper for college students  <sub>[v1 c26 P14](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0014), [v1 c34 P14](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0014)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Phemie  <sub>[v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a diminutive, elderly woman with a small, gently triangular face, rose-colored cheeks, and white hair styled in rolls above her ears. Her big blue eyes possess a youthful sparkle and are full of expectation. She dresses in an outmoded style.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 c22 P10](../source/v01-c22.md#nw-v01-c22-p0010), [v1 c26 P0](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0000)_

## Personality

Aunt Euphemia is cheerful, indulgent, and easy-going. She believes in letting young people enjoy themselves and does not bother to strictly supervise or propriety-check her boarders, preferring her own comfort and relaxed views. She possesses an irrepressible youthfulness of spirit and a bright, forgiving humor, though she can occasionally speak with severe frankness.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 c22 P10](../source/v01-c22.md#nw-v01-c22-p0010), [v1 c24 P9](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0009), [v1 c26 P0](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0000), [v1 c26 P22](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0022)_

- Indulgent and easy-going  <sub>[v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 c26 P0](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0000)</sub>
- Cheerful and youthful  <sub>[v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 c22 P10](../source/v01-c22.md#nw-v01-c22-p0010), [v1 c26 P0](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0000)</sub>

## Abilities

- Excellent cooking and housekeeping skills  <sub>[v1 c26 P14](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0014), [v1 c34 P14](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0014)</sub>
- Knitting delicate items  <sub>[v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 c22 P10](../source/v01-c22.md#nw-v01-c22-p0010)</sub>

## Goals

- To live comfortably and enjoy her retirement years without unnecessary worry  <sub>[v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 c26 P0](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0000)</sub>

## History

After her daughter married and departed for missionary work in India, Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house. Mabel Colby suggested that Euphemia come to Portmaris to act as housekeeper for her, Nell Harcourt, and Honora Hollis in a rented house called Tabby's Place. Euphemia agreed and moved to Portmaris, bringing along her cat, the Sarah-cat, and another named Joseph. She spent the academic year happily managing the household, keeping the girls well-fed, and allowing them full freedom. When the girls left for their summer break, Euphemia chose to stay behind at Tabby's Place to care for the house and the cats, including Smudge, whom Nell had left in her care.

_Sources: [v1 c16 P11](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0011), [v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013), [v1 c26 P14](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0014), [v1 c34 P1](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0001), [v1 c34 P15](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0015)_

## Background by volume

- Her father, named James, drowned at sea a month before she was born, leading to her being named Jamesina  <sub>[v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013)</sub>
- Had a single daughter who married and moved to a foreign mission field in India  <sub>[v1 c16 P11](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0011), [v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013), [v1 c34 P15](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0015)</sub>
- Was widowed after her husband passed away  <sub>[v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013)</sub>

My intention is to be very relaxed here.  <sub>[v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077)</sub>
